subject: Request: Custom SLA addendum + Order Form language for Medion Health (on-call & telemetry)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Rivera <josh.rivera@medionhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@medionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: Custom SLA addendum + Order Form language (Medion)

Hi Josh / Sara,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, attaching our proposed SLA addendum (SLA_Addendum_draft_v2.docx) and the redlines against your MSA (Medion_MSA_redlines_20270522.pdf). High level asks from your side that we want to address in the addendum/order form:

- Explicit uptime commitment for API (regional) and a separate latency SLO for real-time requests (95th / 99th pctl).
- A limited exception window for batched inference (long-tail latency) with defined fallback routing.
- Telemetry / audit export cadence (how often Medion can pull audit logs).
- On-call escalation path and 24x7 vs business-hours coverage.

Can you confirm: 1) whether the procurement team requires service credits structured monthly or quarterly, and 2) the preferred evidence artifacts for SOC2 / uptime investigations?

Proposed next step: we’ll incorporate a short order-form snippet that captures the batched-inference exception + fallback policy and share a DocuSign-ready version by EOD Wednesday if that works.

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_draft_v2.docx, Medion_MSA_redlines_20270522.pdf

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Josh Rivera <josh.rivera@medionhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@medionhealth.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@medionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Custom SLA addendum + Order Form language (Medion)

Michael — thanks for the docs. A few clarifying items from procurement & compliance:

1) Latency SLOs — we need concrete definitions. For the 95th/99th percentile, what request types are included (chat vs long-form generation vs embeddings)? Can you propose separate buckets?

2) Batched inference exception — Medion is open to an exception but wants a maximum allowed percentage of requests/month that can be routed to a degraded mode before credits are triggered.

3) Telemetry & evidence — compliance needs a weekly export of request-level telemetry (anonymized request id, timestamp, region, response time) and a runbook of how Redwood will investigate incidents. SOC2 report is required prior to signature.

4) On-call escalation — we need a 30-minute acknowledgement window for Sev1, with updates every 60 minutes until resolution or workaround.

Procurement asks if Redwood can accept DocuSign for the addendum and whether order form language can include the credit schedule (example: monthly availability < 99.5% => 5% service credit).

I’ve attached Medion_Procurement_Checklist.pdf for reference.

—Josh
Josh Rivera
Head of Cloud Integrations, Medion Health
josh.rivera@medionhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Medion SLA negotiation points

Mike / Kim — quick internal take before we send the consolidated reply: 

- Separate latency buckets by API surface: 1) Low-latency RPC (chat/streaming) 2) Heavy-gen (long-form) 3) Embeddings. Recommend proposing 95th/99th per-bucket.
- For batched exception, suggest a threshold of up to 3% of requests/month routed to degraded/batched mode before credits. Keep routing fallback to same-region read-only variant if possible.
- For credits, propose monthly calculation (simpler for our billing flow). Example draft language we can provide in order form:

  "Availability Credit Schedule: Monthly Availability < 99.5% = 5% credit; < 99.0% = 10% credit. Credits apply to Monthly Invoice for affected Service Region. Credits do not exceed 50% of monthly fees."

- On-call: we can commit to a 30-minute acknowledgement for Sev1 but ask for a joint post-incident review (within 5 business days) as part of evidence.

I’ll mark up the SLA_Addendum_draft_v2 and return v2.1 with the order-form snippet. Want to keep DocuSign flow.

-Marissa
Sr. Manager, Contracts & Procurements | Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Rivera <josh.rivera@medionhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@medionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated proposal: SLA addendum + order form language (Medion)

Josh / Sara — consolidated response and proposed order-form snippets below (see inline). Apologies for the long mail — wanted to be explicit so procurement has copy/paste language.

1) Latency SLOs (per API surface)
- Chat/Streaming: 95th <= 220ms, 99th <= 480ms
- Long-form generation: 95th <= 1.2s, 99th <= 2.8s
- Embeddings: 95th <= 180ms, 99th <= 350ms

2) Batched inference exception
- Exception window: up to 3% of total requests/month may be served under a batched/degraded execution path during periods of constrained capacity.
- Fallback behavior: requests flagged for batching will be routed to a compatible model variant in the same region; users will receive a 1xx advisory in-stream indicating degraded latency.

3) Credits (order form snippet)
- "Availability Credit Schedule: If Monthly Availability for the Service Region falls below 99.5%: Customer will receive a credit equal to 5% of the Monthly Service Fee for the affected Service Region. If Monthly Availability falls below 99.0%: Customer will receive a credit equal to 10% of the Monthly Service Fee for the affected Service Region. Total aggregate credits in a single billing month will not exceed 50% of the Monthly Service Fee."

4) Telemetry & evidence
- Redwood will provide a weekly anonymized telemetry export (CSV) with: request_id, timestamp_utc, region, api_surface, response_ms. SOC2 Type II report will be provided upon execution.
- Incident runbook: Redwood will provide post-incident report within 72 hours of incident mitigation and a joint post-incident review within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents.

5) On-call escalation
- Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge Sev1 incidents within 30 minutes. Status updates every 60 minutes until resolution or workaround. On-call escalation contacts and rotation will be provided prior to go-live.

If this matches Medion expectations we will prepare SLA_Addendum_final.docx and an order-form (single-page) for DocuSign. Please confirm by EOD tomorrow so procurement can route DocuSign for signature this week.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Josh Rivera <josh.rivera@medionhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@medionhealth.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@medionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T14:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated proposal: SLA addendum + order form language (Medion)

Michael — this looks good and is close to what procurement needs. We have three quick asks before DocuSign: 

1) Please confirm the weekly telemetry export will include a stable request_id so we can correlate across infra logs (anonymized is fine).
2) Can the credit calculation exclude scheduled maintenance windows > 4 hours (we will send a maintenance calendar)?
3) Please attach SOC2 Type II (most recent) and confirm estimated time to produce the final SLA_Addendum_final.docx for signature (we prefer by COB tomorrow).

If you can confirm the three points we will route DocuSign and target signature early next week. DocuSign link for procurement intake: https://docusign.com/MDN-1087-SLA

—Josh

Attachments: Medion_Procurement_Checklist.pdf, MDN-redline-questions.xlsx
